subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining request defines new public scheduling semantics and config/API shape, and repository policy treats config/default additions and scheduling contracts as compatibility-sensitive maintainer decisions.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit `every` schedule phase or stagger surface across schema, CLI/tool/protocol, persistence, status/docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve the current `everyMs`/`anchorMs` semantics and treat anti-herd behavior as covered by heartbeat phases plus cron-expression stagger.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus phase controls for heartbeat and cron, with explicit migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` schedule phase or stagger surface across schema, CLI/tool/protocol, persistence, status/docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history on cron stagger semantics and recent schedule-contract extensions.
